title: Human Resources Assistants, Except Payroll and Timekeeping

tasks.short: Explain personnel policies, benefits and procedures to employees and applicants.

steps.what: Read the question and establish its topic and audience.
Find the current policy, benefit terms and applicable procedure.
Check relevant employment facts for an authenticated employee.
Write and send a routine policy explanation.

loop.input: Question, current approved sources and minimum permitted employment context.
loop.output: Plain-language explanation with source references and unresolved points.
loop.check: Require valid source references, matching policy dates and audience permissions; the HR assistant checks meaning before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing or conflicting sources produce a referral rather than an answer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover common questions, but varied questions need a short explanation combining several policy passages.

steps.what: Discuss sensitive circumstances and check that the person understands their options.
Refer unresolved interpretations or exception requests to the HR specialist.
Record the answer, referral and follow-up status.

tasks.design: Use a topic form in the {HELPDESK}, a versioned policy index in the {DOCS} and permission-limited context from the {HCM}. Approved templates handle standard questions; a bounded loop drafts explanations for review before sending through the {EMAIL}. Sensitive conversations remain human, while referrals and case records follow configured workflows.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policies were scattered, versions were unclear and answers depended on individual knowledge. Searching faster alone did not ensure the correct policy applied.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned retrieval, reusable answer templates and bounded drafting can prepare an explanation with traceable sources. Existing request workflows handle routing and follow-up.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting agreements, unusual personal circumstances and exceptions require interpretation. A technically correct answer can still be poorly understood or distressing.
tasks.human_edge: Notice hesitation, explain practical consequences and help someone ask the question they were reluctant to raise.

ambition.what: An asynchronous policy question service for employees working outside office hours.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time searching and more time explaining choices and resolving unclear cases. They can publish reviewed routine explanations within their remit; they cannot grant policy exceptions.

reach.task: Turn recurring policy questions into clearer employee guidance.
reach.learn: Policy interpretation, accessible writing and distinguishing explanation from individual advice.

evidence.claim: HR policy answering from collective agreement material is offered today.
Knowledge-based answering with a prefilled request when no answer is available is offered today.
Direct AI interaction requires the applicable transparency disclosure.
The proposed time savings and service design are estimates; support-centre case results do not establish HR outcomes.

assumptions: Shares blend routine written answers, conversations and referrals; each question need not follow every branch.
A topic form replaces routine intake sorting; unclassified questions enter the human queue.
Applicants receive public policy information without access to employee records.
The first deployment reviews generated explanations before sending.
GDPR access and minimisation requirements apply; national employment rules affect interpretation.
A direct employee-facing AI interface would disclose that it uses AI.
unknowns: Who approves policy versions and resolves conflicting guidance?
Which agreements and employee groups require different answers?
How many questions need personal context or a conversation?
Can employees outside office hours access an authenticated request channel?
research_questions: How should answer evaluation measure omission of exceptions and misleading simplification?
Which national rules constrain individual benefit or employment advice?
new_work: Review generated explanations and maintain approved answer templates.
Withdraw superseded policies from retrieval.
Inspect unanswered questions and referral delays.
Test permissions and source references after policy changes.
tasks.statement: Explain company personnel policies, benefits, and procedures to employees or job applicants.

tasks.short: Update employee data from approved changes, payroll outputs, operational records and supervisory reports.

steps.what: Read employee and manager requests for personnel data changes.
Retrieve approved earnings data for personnel record updates.
Retrieve attributable production or sales totals where personnel records require them.
Match employee identifiers, reporting periods and effective dates in the update workbook.
Enter approved address, absence and other routine employee field changes.
Attach the approved supervisory report to the employee performance record.
Record the authorised termination date and reason.
Check saved fields against the approved change set.
Confirm completion to the authorised requester.

tasks.design: Configure authenticated change forms and field ownership in the {HCM}; use deterministic adapters for required data from the {PAYROLL} and {OPS_SYSTEM}. Match identifiers and effective dates before writing, preserve source references, and link approved reports in the {TALENT}. Reconcile writes automatically and gate termination activation with the HR specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate identifiers, effective dates and batch exports made copying easier than maintaining reliable interfaces. Unclear field ownership encouraged duplicate records.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured self-service handles routine changes, and reusable adapters can enforce matching, validation and replay protection. AI-assisted coding can shorten implementation without introducing a model into record updates.
tasks.still_hard: Retroactive corrections, rehires, multiple contracts and termination reversals complicate effective dating. Some earnings and production fields may have no valid reason to be duplicated.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve conflicting authoritative sources and recognise when a routine-looking update could wrongly affect employment or pay.

ambition.what: A daily correction queue for conflicting employee effective dates.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends more time resolving source conflicts and less time copying values. They can request corrections from source owners under agreed rules; they gain no authority to change pay or decide termination.

reach.task: Investigate employee master-data differences before a pay run.
reach.learn: Effective dating, payroll cutoffs and correction versus reversal.

evidence.claim: Configured HR self-service changes can flow into payroll.
Identifier matching, effective-date checks and write reconciliation can use deterministic code.
The proposed workflow records authorised outcomes rather than making termination or performance decisions.
Time shares, remaining effort and delivery ranges are estimates requiring local validation.

assumptions: Source retrieval steps apply only to employee groups needing those fields.
Earnings are copied from approved results; the assistant does not calculate payroll.
The example company uses the {OPS_SYSTEM} for attributable output; other companies may use the {CRM}.
The structured-data prior supports deterministic updates; system screens receive more weight than the supplied document-time prior.
Routine changes use authenticated requests and existing approvals where required.
Unnecessary duplicate fields should be removed after confirming recordkeeping needs.
National consultation requirements and access provisioning are included where applicable.
unknowns: Which employee fields must legally and operationally be retained?
Which system is authoritative for each field?
Are reliable employee identifiers and effective-dated interfaces available?
Do termination updates trigger account removal or other downstream actions?
How often do retroactive corrections and rehires occur?
research_questions: Which national recordkeeping duties require earnings or production data in personnel records?
Which adapter patterns safely handle multiple concurrent employment contracts?
new_work: Resolve identifier, period and effective-date exceptions.
Maintain source ownership and field mappings.
Check interface failures, duplicate events and unauthorised field changes.
Review termination activation and downstream reconciliation.
tasks.statement: Record data for each employee, including such information as addresses, weekly earnings, absences, amount of sales or production, supervisory reports on performance, and dates of and reasons for terminations.

tasks.short: Check applications, assemble qualification evidence and support human screening decisions.

steps.what: Check incoming applications for required fields, attachments and duplicate submissions.
Read application documents and identify stated qualifications and supporting evidence.

loop.input: Application documents and a fixed qualification-evidence schema
loop.output: Stated qualifications with document references and explicit unknown fields
loop.check: Validate the schema and source references; a reviewer checks facts used in screening.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per application; unreadable or conflicting documents go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Qualifications appear in varied free-text documents that fixed field mapping cannot reliably read.

steps.what: Compare evidence with approved job criteria and note gaps or unclear equivalences.
Ask the applicant for specific missing facts or supporting documents.
Evaluate relevant evidence and decide whether the applicant should progress.
Record the approved outcome and its evidence-based reason in the applicant record.
Send the approved outcome or next-step invitation to the applicant.

tasks.design: Configure completeness checks and candidate communications in the {ATS}, with a bounded extraction loop producing cited qualification evidence from application documents. Deterministic code creates a criterion-by-criterion screening brief without ranking candidates; the recruiter approves progression decisions and external outcome messages before the {WORKFLOW} records and sends them.
tasks.previous_blocker: Applications use inconsistent language, while qualification equivalence and relevant experience resist fixed rules. Earlier automation risked treating missing evidence as a negative decision.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction can expose source evidence and uncertainty, while configured workflows handle completeness and paperwork. The judgement step remains human, so implementation does not depend on reliable automated candidate selection.
tasks.still_hard: Equivalent qualifications, career gaps, accessibility and unequal evidence quality require context. GDPR applies, and intended-purpose assessment must establish the relevant EU AI Act obligations; national employment and consultation rules vary.
tasks.human_edge: Judge relevant evidence fairly, recognize alternative routes to qualification and give defensible reasons for progression decisions.

ambition.what: Applicants with nonstandard qualifications receiving an explicit equivalence review

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time copying qualifications and more time obtaining missing evidence and preparing difficult cases. They can route nonstandard qualifications for equivalence review; the recruiter retains progression and rejection authority.

reach.task: Assess qualification equivalence for recruitment
reach.learn: Job analysis, evidence standards and recognition of alternative qualifications

reach.task: Review screening criteria and outcomes for unequal treatment
reach.learn: Criterion validation, selection-process documentation and interpretation of group comparisons

evidence.claim: Applicant matching with a recruiter decision is an existing HR software capability.
Recruitment and candidate-selection AI appear in the EU AI Act high-risk categories.
A procedural exception requires assessment; profiling does not qualify for that exception.
GDPR Article 22 limits solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, subject to specified exceptions.
Cited extraction and fixed criterion tables can reduce preparation work without automating selection.

assumptions: Job criteria are approved before applications are reviewed.
The proposed system extracts stated evidence and does not infer personality, protected traits or candidate scores.
Missing evidence produces a clarification item, not an automatic rejection.
A substantive recruiter review is required; a nominal approval alone is insufficient.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates; the judgement-heavy prior supports retaining the decision step.
Consultation and access ranges cover initial review; additional obligations may extend delivery.
unknowns: Current screening criteria and treatment of qualification equivalence
Actual decision rights and approval requirements
Whether existing screening uses rankings, profiling or automatic rejection
Application languages, document quality and accessibility needs
Interfaces, model access permissions and applicable national consultation requirements
research_questions: Can factual extraction remain separate from evaluative scoring in the actual implementation?
How often does extraction omit relevant evidence or misstate a qualification?
Which equivalence questions require a specialist rather than fixed rules?
What EU AI Act classification and obligations follow from the intended use?
new_work: Review extracted facts and source references
Resolve qualification equivalence and missing-evidence cases
Approve progression decisions and candidate messages
Maintain criteria, extraction schemas and clarification templates
Monitor extraction errors and patterns of unequal treatment
Maintain required assessment records and candidate-data retention controls
tasks.statement: Process and review employment applications to evaluate qualifications or eligibility of applicants.

tasks.short: Answer employee and applicant questions about examinations, eligibility, salaries, benefits and HR procedures.

steps.what: Read the question and verify identity, scope and access rights.
Look up relevant employee or applicant facts.
Find current policies, benefit rules and examination guidance.
Combine personnel facts and guidance into a proposed answer.

loop.input: Authorised question, permitted personnel facts and current approved guidance.
loop.output: Draft answer with source references and explicit unresolved points.
loop.check: Validate source versions, references and numerical fields; reject unsupported entitlement conclusions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; missing or conflicting support routes to an HR specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover fixed questions; varied wording and contextual explanations need bounded drafting.

steps.what: Resolve ambiguous eligibility or policy interpretations when needed.
Check the answer, send it and record the response.

tasks.design: An authenticated answer desk in the {WORKFLOW} retrieves permitted facts from the {HCM} or {ATS} and current guidance from the {DOCS}. Fixed answers use templates; a bounded drafting loop prepares contextual replies with references. An HR specialist approves ambiguous interpretations, and the HR assistant approves release through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Guidance, personal facts and correspondence sit separately. Maintaining current guidance and access rights takes more effort than building a search box.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing self-service and knowledge features cover much of the flow. AI-assisted coding reduces connector and validation work; bounded drafting handles varied wording.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting agreements, individual exceptions and outdated guidance remain difficult. GDPR access controls, EU AI Act classification and applicable national rules need assessment when the scope changes.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a factual question hides distress, a dispute or a request for discretion.

ambition.what: An employee benefit-change explainer using approved personal facts.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward difficult questions and repairing confusing guidance. No entitlement decision rights change; a delegated role could propose guidance changes from recurring questions.

reach.task: Explain benefit eligibility exceptions.
reach.learn: Effective dates, agreement precedence and when an explanation becomes an entitlement decision.

evidence.claim: HR self-service and answers grounded in employment agreements are available capabilities.
Knowledge-based answers can hand unresolved questions to a pre-filled request.
Personalised salary and eligibility replies need access restrictions and controlled release.

assumptions: Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured results.
The employer has searchable guidance and employee records with identifiable effective dates.
Specialist handling is conditional; its share represents time across a typical mix of inquiries.
The final handoff includes applicants; employee replies remain internal.
Build ranges are working-day effort for one deployment. Access includes consultation under national rules where applicable; elapsed waiting time may be longer.
unknowns: Which guidance is approved, current and owned?
Which inquiry types require specialist interpretation?
Can existing authentication and record permissions be reused?
Which consultation and access approvals apply locally?
research_questions: How reliably do existing knowledge features filter guidance by agreement and effective date?
Which additional EU AI Act obligations apply if the scope moves from explanation into employment decisions?
new_work: Review drafted replies and resolve unsupported statements.
Maintain guidance versions, answer templates and escalation routes.
Investigate access failures and sample released answers for accuracy.
tasks.statement: Answer questions regarding examinations, eligibility, salaries, benefits, and other pertinent information.

tasks.short: Search employee files and provide authorised facts for inquiries and personnel actions.

steps.what: Read the inquiry and clarify the facts needed.
Verify the requester's authority and permitted information scope.
Retrieve relevant dates, roles, contract fields and recorded changes.
Read relevant contracts, letters and supporting employee-file documents.

loop.input: Authorised question and permission-filtered employee-file documents.
loop.output: Relevant factual extracts with document, page and effective-date references.
loop.check: Confirm quotations against source text and validate employee identity and document version.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; absent or conflicting evidence is returned as unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured fields use direct lookup; facts in varied historical letters need contextual extraction.

steps.what: Reconcile conflicting records and identify facts requiring specialist confirmation.
Check disclosure scope, send the fact brief and record the disclosure.

tasks.design: A request form in the {WORKFLOW} checks identity and disclosure scope before retrieving structured facts from the {HCM}. Permission-filtered documents from the {DOCS} feed a bounded extraction loop, and a deterministic generator assembles a cited fact brief. The HR assistant resolves conflicts and approves disclosure; the brief supports a separately authorised personnel decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Structured records and historical letters disagree or use different dates. Broad folder access makes safe retrieval harder than simple search.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record views can answer structured questions directly. Small integrations and cited text extraction reduce document reading and brief assembly.
tasks.still_hard: Historical contradictions and unclear authority cannot be settled by retrieval. GDPR purpose limits, sensitive records, EU AI Act scope and applicable national rules remain relevant.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a documented fact from an inference and recognise when releasing a true fact would still be inappropriate.

ambition.what: An evidence brief showing effective dates and unresolved conflicts before contract changes.

tasks.altitude: The assistant becomes a stronger evidence partner for HR specialists and spends less time searching files. Employment decision rights do not change; disputed facts still need authorised resolution.

reach.task: Build an evidence chronology for a disputed personnel action.
reach.learn: Source provenance, neutral chronology, confidentiality and the boundary between fact and interpretation.

evidence.claim: Existing HR systems support employee records and self-service information flows.
Permission-filtered retrieval and source-cited extraction can support factual briefs without deciding personnel actions.
Record conflicts and disclosure scope need explicit handling before information is released.

assumptions: Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured results.
Most requests seek internal factual information rather than legal advice.
The request form replaces much of mailbox clarification; unusual requests still need a person.
Retrieval permissions are enforced before document content reaches the model.
Unresolved conflicts remain visible and are not silently resolved by document recency.
Build ranges are working-day effort. Access includes consultation under national rules where applicable; elapsed waiting time may be longer.
unknowns: Are document permissions as granular as employee-record permissions?
Which source prevails for each personnel field and effective date?
Who may resolve conflicting records or approve unusual disclosures?
How much of the archive is searchable and correctly indexed?
Which local consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Can retrieval preserve document-level permissions across both current files and archives?
How accurately can extraction distinguish signed amendments from superseded drafts?
new_work: Review cited extracts and investigate conflicting records.
Maintain field ownership, disclosure rules and permission mappings.
Audit disclosure logs and correct indexing or source-version errors.
tasks.statement: Examine employee files to answer inquiries and provide information for personnel actions.

tasks.short: Collect required personnel records from employees and departments, check completeness and file them.

steps.what: Identify required records for the employee event.
Find records already held by HR and other departments.
Request missing records from employees or departmental owners.
Receive submitted records and record receipt.
Check document identity, dates, completeness and apparent inconsistencies.

loop.input: Submitted documents, required fields and permitted employee identifiers.
loop.output: Document type, cited field values and completeness exceptions.
loop.check: Validate identifiers, date formats and required fields against the checklist; a person reviews uncertain matches.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unreadable or conflicting documents enter the exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Forms need only fixed validation; varied legacy documents require bounded text extraction.

steps.what: Chase outstanding records and clarify incomplete submissions.
Attach accepted records to the employee file and close the collection checklist.

tasks.design: An event in the {HCM} selects a required-record checklist and reuses permitted records from the {HCM}, {LMS} and {DOCS}. Configured self-service uploads replace attachment handling, while a bounded extraction loop checks legacy documents for review. The {WORKFLOW} sends capped reminders, routes exceptions and files accepted records with an audit trail.
tasks.previous_blocker: Record requirements and ownership vary by event. Mail attachments lack reliable identifiers, and departments keep separate copies.
tasks.enabler_now: Self-service capture and deterministic record matching cover the main flow. Bounded extraction reduces manual inspection of varied documents.
tasks.still_hard: Missing records still require their owners to act. Authenticity, disputed facts, special-category data and retention rules need human handling under GDPR and applicable national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Understand why someone cannot provide a record and agree a legitimate alternative without collecting unnecessary information.

ambition.what: A pre-action personnel-record readiness check for HR specialists.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends more time resolving evidence gaps before employment changes are delayed. No employment decision rights change; delegated discretion could cover requesting approved alternative evidence.

reach.task: Check whether personnel evidence supports a proposed contract change.
reach.learn: Evidence sufficiency, agreement requirements and escalation for disputed records.

evidence.claim: HR self-service can collect changes and route them into connected employee administration.
Document extraction with rule checks and exception routing is an available pattern; HR-specific validation needs testing.
Existing records can be reused through permission-controlled references instead of repeated collection.

assumptions: Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured results.
Shares measure collection administration; employees' time finding or producing missing evidence is excluded.
The checklist specifies permitted record types, required fields and retention rules.
The model checks document content, not authenticity or employment eligibility.
Reminders stop after two attempts and escalate unresolved cases.
Build ranges are working-day effort. Access includes consultation under national rules where applicable; elapsed waiting time may be longer.
unknowns: Which employee events trigger each checklist?
Where are authoritative records held and who may access them?
What proportion of submissions use structured forms versus varied documents?
Which records require specialist verification or restricted storage?
Which consultation requirements apply locally?
research_questions: What extraction accuracy can representative redacted personnel documents support?
Can existing self-service preserve document versions and prevent duplicate filing?
new_work: Review uncertain document matches and disputed submissions.
Maintain checklists, record ownership and reminder schedules.
Repair failed transfers and audit duplicate or incorrectly retained records.
tasks.statement: Gather personnel records from other departments or employees.

tasks.short: Find personnel information and disclose permitted facts to authorized requesters.

steps.what: Receive the request and identify the employee and requested information.
Check requester identity, authority, purpose and permitted fields against disclosure rules.
Look up permitted employment facts in the employee record.
Find supporting contracts or letters in the personnel file.
Prepare a response containing only authorized facts and attachments.
Check facts, attachments and recipient, then release the response.
File the released response and record its recipient and authorization.

tasks.design: Configure request intake in the {WORKFLOW}, with field-level retrieval from the {HCM} and indexed files in the {DOCS}. A deterministic generator prepares the permitted disclosure; the HR specialist approves external release through the {EMAIL}, and the {WORKFLOW} records the disclosure log.
tasks.previous_blocker: Authorization evidence sits apart from personnel records. Inconsistent file names and broad access permissions make safe retrieval difficult.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, access controls and document indexes cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting them; no model is needed for standard disclosures.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous authority, old scanned files and conflicting records require investigation. GDPR lawful basis, minimization and access controls apply; national rules may add requirements.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when a plausible request exceeds the requester's authority and explain a refusal without damaging trust.

ambition.what: Employee-requested employment verification with visible request status

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time searching and more time resolving authorization and record conflicts. They can manage standard verification cases within an approved disclosure policy; authority over exceptional disclosures remains with the HR specialist.

reach.task: Resolve disputed employment verification requests
reach.learn: Lawful disclosure grounds, identity checks and conflicting-record investigation

evidence.claim: Employee self-service and connected HR records are existing capabilities.
Permission-filtered retrieval, template disclosures and audit logging can use deterministic technology.
GDPR Article 22 concerns consequential automated decisions; disclosure authorization also needs separate privacy controls.

assumptions: A typical company keeps current facts in the {HCM} and supporting files in the {DOCS}.
The proposed first release covers standard employment facts, not unrestricted personnel-file access.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.
The document-heavy prior is retained; structured retrieval does not remove authorization judgement.
unknowns: Which request types are permitted and who approves them
Whether employee identifiers link the {HCM} and the {DOCS}
How many files are scanned, unindexed or contradictory
Available interfaces, access permissions and national consultation requirements
research_questions: Can existing permissions filter individual fields and attachments before retrieval?
Which standard disclosures can be generated entirely from authoritative structured facts?
new_work: Review disclosure drafts and recipient identity
Handle disputed authority and conflicting records
Maintain disclosure templates, field permissions and document indexing
Check failed deliveries and disclosure-log completeness
tasks.statement: Search employee files to obtain information for authorized persons and organizations, such as credit bureaus and finance companies.

tasks.short: Interview applicants, verify relevant facts and record evidence for the recruiter.

steps.what: Review the application and screening brief before arranging an interview.
Agree an interview time and send the applicant practical joining information.
Prepare job-related questions about missing facts and unclear application statements.

loop.input: Application passages, approved job criteria, missing facts and approved question library
loop.output: Proposed clarification questions with source references
loop.check: Require a job criterion and application reference for each question; the interviewer checks relevance.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt per guide; unresolved items use the question library.
loop.why_not_simpler: Unclear free-text claims need contextual clarification that fixed questions cannot always express.

steps.what: Interview the applicant, clarify facts and answer questions about the process.
Check supplied evidence and resolve discrepancies in relevant applicant facts.
Write a factual interview summary and update the applicant record.

loop.input: Interviewer-entered notes, verified facts and unresolved discrepancies
loop.output: Factual summary separating verified facts, applicant statements and unresolved questions
loop.check: Every statement must trace to a note or evidence item; the interviewer approves the record update.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; use a structured manual summary if checks fail.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text interview notes need condensation while preserving qualifications and uncertainty.

steps.what: Give the recruiter a recommendation and identify facts still needing investigation.

tasks.design: Configure scheduling through the {ATS} and {CALENDAR}, and generate an interview guide from approved criteria and applicant evidence. Small bounded loops draft clarification questions and summarize interviewer-entered notes; the interviewer approves these artefacts, conducts the conversation and supplies a human recommendation in the {ATS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Interview preparation and summaries depend on varied application text and personal notes. The conversation itself requires trust and responsive questioning.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduling is already configurable, and bounded drafting can work from a small evidence packet with explicit checks. This reduces preparation and paperwork without requiring automated interviewing.
tasks.still_hard: Authenticity checks, accommodations and ambiguous answers remain human work. GDPR applies; recruitment-related AI needs an EU AI Act intended-purpose assessment, and employee consultation follows national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Build enough trust for applicants to clarify uncertainty, ask fair follow-up questions and distinguish missing evidence from lack of ability.

ambition.what: Candidate clarification appointments before recruiter review

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends more of the week interviewing and resolving unclear evidence, with shorter preparation and write-up periods. They can offer clarification appointments within the recruitment process; hiring decision rights remain with the recruiter and hiring manager.

reach.task: Conduct structured candidate interviews
reach.learn: Evidence-based questioning, reasonable accommodations and consistent interview documentation

reach.task: Review interview questions for unequal treatment
reach.learn: Job relevance, sensitive-information boundaries and accessible interview practices

evidence.claim: Existing HR software supports applicant matching with the recruiter retaining the decision.
Bounded drafting can assist interview preparation and factual summaries; this digest provides no HR interview case.
Recruitment AI can fall within the EU AI Act high-risk category.
The narrow procedural exception depends on the intended use; profiling is excluded from that exception.

assumptions: The assistant gathers and verifies facts; the recruiter makes selection decisions.
Summaries use interviewer-entered notes, with no automatic recording or emotion inference.
The interview remains the largest step, consistent with the human-conversation prior.
Invitations use approved logistics and candidate-selected availability.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates, including intended-purpose review and applicable consultation.
unknowns: Who interviews, recommends and makes selection decisions
Current question library and interview documentation standard
Candidate accommodation process and languages required
Permitted model processing location, retention and access
Applicable national consultation requirements
research_questions: Does drafting improve factual coverage without introducing unsupported claims?
Can the existing {ATS} handle scheduling and structured notes through configuration?
Does the intended use remain procedural or materially influence candidate evaluation?
new_work: Review questions and summaries against source evidence
Handle scheduling and accommodation exceptions
Maintain approved questions and summary checks
Monitor unsupported statements and inappropriate questions
Reassess the intended use when recruitment features change
tasks.statement: Interview job applicants to obtain and verify information used to screen and evaluate them.

tasks.short: Obtain authorised applicant references and background-check information for a human hiring assessment.

steps.what: Confirm which reference and background checks are necessary and legally permitted.
Obtain required applicant notices, referee details and any necessary authorisation.
Send approved reference requests or submit an authorised official-check request.
Discuss job-related reference questions with the referee by telephone.
Chase outstanding replies and record unavailable or declined checks.
Check response identity, completeness and discrepancies; assemble the restricted check file.
Assess discrepancies and refer relevant findings to the authorised hiring decision-maker.

tasks.design: Configure a restricted check register in the {ATS} or {WORKFLOW}, with approved scope, notices, request templates, deadlines and retention controls. Send only authorised requests and bounded reminders through {EMAIL}; store necessary evidence with restricted access in {DOCS}. Remove unnecessary checks at scope review, while people conduct reference conversations, verify discrepancies and assess findings.
tasks.previous_blocker: External replies arrive through varied channels, and permissible checks differ by role and national rules. Sensitive information was often tracked through individual mailboxes.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, request templates, reminder rules and restricted records already cover much of the coordination. Small connections can bring status into one register without automating the hiring assessment.
tasks.still_hard: Referee identity, incomplete responses and disputed statements require investigation. Criminal-record information has specific GDPR restrictions, and candidate permission alone does not establish that a check is lawful.
tasks.human_edge: Ask proportionate questions, distinguish facts from opinion and give applicants a fair chance to address discrepancies.

ambition.what: Provide a documented applicant discrepancy-resolution process before adverse findings reach a hiring decision.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time chasing replies and more time resolving evidence gaps with applicants and referees. They coordinate the discrepancy process; the specialist and hiring manager retain assessment and hiring authority.

reach.task: Review disputed pre-employment check findings.
reach.learn: Evidence provenance, proportionate checks, applicant correction rights and escalation under national rules.

evidence.claim: Request templates, bounded reminders and restricted check registers can use existing workflow features.
GDPR Article 10 specifically restricts processing of criminal-conviction and offence data; national authorisation requirements vary.
GDPR Article 22 constrains solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
Human conversations and assessments can remain manual while their preparation and coordination are automated.

assumptions: Step shares average a mixed caseload; official checks and telephone references do not occur in every case.
Routine European practice centres on proportionate references and permitted checks, rather than unrestricted enquiries to law enforcement.
The baseline uses written requests; mandatory portal or paper routes require separate local steps and effort estimates.
Unnecessary checks are omitted at scope review rather than created as a separate recurring step.
Reminders repeat an already approved request, disclose no additional information, have a fixed limit and stop on reply or withdrawal.
No model processes reference or criminal-record content in this design.
Build ranges include privacy review, restricted access and applicable national employee consultation.
unknowns: Which checks are legally required or permitted for the roles and countries involved.
Whether official information must be supplied by the applicant or obtained through an authorised route.
Which requests require a portal, paper form or verified identity.
Who can access findings and how long each evidence category must be retained.
Whether the {ATS} can restrict sensitive check evidence separately from ordinary candidate records.
Who has authority to resolve disputed findings and pause a hiring decision.
research_questions: Which existing checks lack a documented necessity or permitted basis?
Which response channels create the most chasing and identity-verification work?
Can the register retain a necessary check outcome without retaining excessive underlying information?
new_work: Maintain permitted-check policies by role and applicable national rules.
Handle failed requests, unavailable referees and portal exceptions.
Review discrepancies with applicants and specialists.
Audit access and enforce evidence-retention rules.
Maintain reminder limits and stop conditions.
tasks.statement: Request information from law enforcement officials, previous employers, and other references to determine applicants' employment acceptability.

tasks.short: Compile personnel data into reports and supporting documents for authorized internal users.

steps.what: Confirm the reporting period, definitions, required fields and recipients.
Export employee and training records for the agreed reporting period.
Join exports, reconcile totals and identify missing or inconsistent records.
Ask record owners to confirm exceptions and supply corrected source records.
Populate report tables and standard personnel documents from corrected data.
Review definitions, totals, sensitive details and the proposed recipient list.
Publish the approved report and notify its authorized recipients.

tasks.design: Scheduled jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM} join authorized exports from the {HCM} and {LMS}, validate totals and route exceptions through the {WORKFLOW}. A deterministic generator creates reports in the {DOCS} and refreshes the {BI}; approved reports are distributed to a controlled recipient list.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different definitions, reporting dates and identifiers made each reporting pack a manual reconciliation exercise.

tasks.statement: Prepare and set up for new employee orientations.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts toward resolving record conflicts, preparing sound cases and explaining procedures. Administrative correction rights can expand within agreed limits; employment, benefit and claim decisions stay with authorised decision-makers.
reach: Human Resources Specialists: prepare evidence-based case chronologies and clearer policy guidance.
Payroll and Timekeeping Clerks: investigate effective-date and employee master-data mismatches.
Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists: reconcile provider enrolments and contribution instructions.
skills_to_grow: Effective dating, source ownership and record reconciliation.
Privacy-aware document handling and permission design.
Reviewing extracted fields and source-backed explanations.
Policy interpretation, employee communication and escalation.
Maintaining workflow rules and investigating integration failures.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide a personnel administration readiness service that catches incomplete cases, conflicting dates and approaching benefit deadlines before they harm employees. Reusable templates provide a head start across employers, with local policies, access and national rules configured for each deployment.

role_batches.altitude: The week shifts from searching, chasing and assembling toward evidence quality, difficult inquiries and starter readiness. Greater authority requires explicit delegation; these changes do not confer employment decision rights.
reach: HR specialists: prepare evidence for contract changes.
Compensation and benefits specialists: explain eligibility exceptions.
Training and development specialists: improve accessible induction preparation.
Labor relations specialists: assemble neutral personnel chronologies.
skills_to_grow: Effective dates, source precedence and personnel evidence quality.
GDPR-aware access, disclosure and retention practices.
Workflow configuration, exception handling and integration monitoring.
Checking source-cited model outputs without accepting unsupported conclusions.
Accessible communication and sensitive employee conversations.
role_batches.ambitious_version: An HR operations evidence partner who provides timely, permission-controlled facts and spots recurring preparation gaps before they delay employee changes or onboarding.

role_batches.altitude: The HR assistant's week shifts from retrieval, copying and report assembly toward evidence checking, applicant conversations and difficult record cases. They gain bounded authority to manage clarification and correction queues; disclosure exceptions, recruitment decisions and HR policy remain with the responsible specialists and managers.
reach: Human Resources Specialists: qualification equivalence and disputed personnel records
Human Resources Managers: interpretation of personnel trends
Training and Development Specialists: reconciliation of training evidence
Equal Opportunity Representatives: review of interview and screening practices
skills_to_grow: Permission-aware personnel-data handling
Record reconciliation and metric definitions
Structured interviewing and evidence-based documentation
Qualification equivalence and fair screening
Validation of model drafts against source evidence
Workflow exception investigation
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide a reusable personnel-evidence service: employment verification, reporting, application clarification and interview documentation, with visible status and explicit human decision points. Each organization connects its systems and sets its permissions, definitions and national requirements.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts from repeated entry, publication and chasing toward candidate communication, evidence verification and exception coordination. Hiring, screening-policy and sensitive-check decisions remain with explicitly authorised people.
reach: Human Resources Specialists: review transferable experience and disputed check evidence.
Equal Opportunity Representatives and Officers: investigate recurring barriers in screening.
Human Resources Managers: assess candidate communication and recruitment-process exceptions.
skills_to_grow: Configure forms, templates, approval rules and bounded reminders.
Read integration logs and resolve failed handoffs.
Verify source evidence and recognise unsupported model extraction.
Conduct fair candidate and referee conversations.
Apply GDPR, recruitment AI requirements and relevant national rules.
Analyse process outcomes without turning administrative indicators into hiring scores.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Become a recruitment operations coordinator who runs a candidate discrepancy-resolution service, improves internal vacancy access and brings evidence about recurring process failures to HR specialists.

role_batches.altitude: The assistant shifts from copying records and chasing coordination to preparing reliable cases, resolving exceptions, and supporting employees. New discretion concerns readiness, scheduling proposals, and procedural escalation; assessment interpretation, access permissions, and spending remain with authorised roles.
reach: HR specialist: assessment administration quality and starter readiness.
Training and development specialist: course suitability and accessible cohort planning.
skills_to_grow: Configure forms, approvals, permissions, and retention rules.
Map employee identifiers and reconcile records across systems.
Check source evidence, scoring flags, and extracted contractual terms.
Understand assessment protocols, accessibility, and escalation boundaries.
Translate learning needs into practical scheduling constraints.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run an employee readiness service spanning assessment preparation, workplace access, and accessible training, with clear escalation to qualified specialists and authorised decision makers.
